nodes.long_description:
🚀 LUNAR LANDER

Descend from orbit and attempt a controlled landing on the Moon. Balance thrust, fuel, and velocity as you guide your lander through a tense, high-risk descent. Inspired by classic arcade gameplay, rebuilt for immersive VR.

🎮 Precision Landing Gameplay

Take full control of your descent using thrusters and careful timing.
Every movement matters — too fast and you crash, too slow and you drift off course.

Master:

Thrust control and momentum
Fuel management under pressure
Safe landing speeds and angles
Controlled descents from high altitude
🌑 High-Risk, High-Reward

No two landings feel the same.

Push your limits:

Attempt perfect landings with minimal velocity
Conserve fuel for efficiency bonuses
Recover from unstable descents
Take risks… or play it safe
🧠 Easy to Learn, Hard to Master

Simple controls make it easy to start.
True mastery takes precision, timing, and nerve.

Instant restart gameplay loop
Skill-based progression
Increasing challenge as you improve
🕹️ Retro Arcade, Rebuilt for VR

Inspired by the classic Lunar Lander experience, now fully immersive.

Clean, readable HUD (ALT, FUEL, VEL)
High-contrast visuals designed for VR clarity
Smooth, responsive controls
Focused, distraction-free gameplay
🏆 Challenge Yourself

Can you:

Land perfectly?
Save fuel?
Recover from the edge of disaster?

Or will gravity win?

🌌 Built for VR

Designed specifically for standalone VR:

Comfortable seated gameplay
Clear visual feedback
Fast sessions, perfect for repeat runs
{2030666394147829}

# Lunar Lander VR — Release 1.7.0

## What's New

### Windows and PC Platforms
- Added a central platform layer (`LLVRPlatform`) that identifies Quest standalone, Meta Quest Link, Microsoft Store, SteamVR, and plain Windows desktop builds, so store- and runtime-specific behaviour lives in one place.
- Added **Meta Quest Link (PC)** builds with an entitlement check: release builds stay blocked until the Meta Platform entitlement succeeds, while development builds bypass it with a clear warning.
- Added **Microsoft Store** builds with MSIX identity and cached Store licence validation, including retries and distinct states for unlicensed, trial, and missing-package-identity cases.
- Added Windows build tooling: Meta Quest PC and Microsoft Store editor build menus, a camera build validator, and `tools/` scripts for staging and packaging a Store MSIX and for building all PC targets in batch.
- Standalone Windows package identity updated to `ltd.saxcompute.lunarlandar`.

### Xbox / Gamepad Controls (Windows Desktop and Store)
- Flat Windows builds always use stick flight controls: left stick for throttle and yaw, right stick for pitch and roll, left trigger for direct engine throttle.
- Gamepad **A** toggles cockpit and spectator views; **Y** returns to the menu.
- Added an Xbox controller panel to the instructions, with D-pad / left-stick menu navigation (A to select, B to go back) and an automatic initial menu selection when a gamepad is connected.
- The control-type menu is locked to sticks on Windows; your saved Meta preference is kept and comes back in Quest builds.
- If the serialized flight input actions are missing or incomplete, portable XR and keyboard/gamepad fallback bindings are created at runtime.

### Camera
- Chase view now works on every platform; the Windows cockpit correction no longer forces the camera back to the cockpit view.
- Quest standalone and PCVR keep rendering through the tracked XR camera; Windows uses the spectator camera.

### Quest Age Checks and Leaderboards
- Online leaderboards and PlayFab score submission are now limited to players the Meta age check confirms as eligible.
- Players who are restricted, or whose age check is pending or fails, get **LOCAL SCORES** and a status message instead (checking, retrying, or unavailable). Nothing is sent online for them.
- When the age check resolves as eligible, PlayFab login resumes automatically and the leaderboard refreshes.
- Local score history is now saved on-device on Quest and persists between sessions.
- The leaderboard now follows the selected difficulty, and empty player names show as "You".
- Added `tools/QuestAgeChecks`, a console test harness that runs the production `MetaUserProvider` against Unity/Meta SDK doubles.
Built up terrain around yellow pads

# Lunar Lander VR — Release 1.6.0

## What's New

### Bonus Landing Runs
- Successful landings no longer end the game. The result message now shows points earned, the running total, and **Bonus — Go Again!** before starting another attempt.
- The shuttle respawns at a random safe location above the lunar terrain, away from the map edges.
- Remaining fuel carries into each bonus attempt, turning fuel into the limiting factor for an extended run.
- A successfully claimed landing pad is removed for the rest of the run, encouraging players to explore and hunt for unused targets.
- Crashes still end the run and return to the menu, now showing the accumulated session score.

### Difficulty and Scoring Clarity
- Fixed difficulty selection so it now controls the real maximum safe total impact speed:
  - **Easy:** up to 3 m/s
  - **Medium:** up to 2 m/s
  - **Hard:** up to 1 m/s
- Expanded the right menu panel with colour-matched level limits, pad rewards, fuel-bonus details, and separate-leaderboard information.
- Easy, Medium, and Hard use the same green, amber, and red language as their corresponding pad rewards.

### Music, Thrusters, and Volume Controls
- Added persistent looping menu music that continues into gameplay when enabled.
- Added Music and SFX volume sliders; values and toggle states persist between scenes and sessions.
- Restored throttle-responsive looping thruster audio with configurable clip, maximum volume, and fade time.
- Thruster volume now respects the menu SFX setting.

### VR Comfort and Camera Controls
- Added automatic headset recentering when both the menu and game scenes start, including an application-origin fallback for Meta/OpenXR runtimes that ignore a standard recenter request.
- Adjusted the cockpit viewpoint upward and rearward for a more natural seated position inside the shuttle.
- The **X button** now toggles between cockpit and spectator views; the spectator camera automatically shares the shuttle input-action asset.
- Added X and Y button descriptions to the controls panel. Y returns to the menu.

### Menu Presentation
- Added a matching dark background to the right instructions panel.
- Expanded and resized the instructions layout to accommodate controls, difficulty rules, and scoring information.
- Unified project-owned logging through `LLVRLog` for consistent filtered diagnostics on Quest.

### Quest Build Version
- Updated the Meta Quest application version to **v1.6.0** with Android version code **160**.
